subject: RE: Pricing exhibit — bucket alignment & floor language
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@orionplatform.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@orionplatform.com>
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing exhibit — bucket alignment request

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement ran the forecast against your proposed schedule and flagged three items that need alignment before we can move to signatures:

1) Fee buckets: our forecasted usage sits near the boundary between Band B and Band C; the steep step creates a 45% effective cost jump. Can we smooth the ladder or add a catchband to avoid a cliff?
2) Minimum floor: the exhibit currently has a 12-month minimum tied to committed throughput. Our legal asks for a one-quarter carveout for pilot months with attenuated penalties.
3) True-up cadence: prefer quarterly true-ups versus annual to avoid big reconciliations.

I've attached the forecast and a suggested spreadsheet with proposed bucket midpoints (pricing_exhibit_v3.xlsx). Can your legal team accept a short form amendment or do you need an updated exhibit with redlines?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our steering committee meets Friday.

Best,
Jordan Ellis
Lead, Strategic Sourcing
Orion Platform

Attachments: pricing_exhibit_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@orionplatform.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Pricing exhibit — bucket alignment request

Jordan, thanks for the fast read and the spreadsheet — useful.

Quick answers:
- We can produce a redlined exhibit that smooths the bucket boundaries and adds a transitional band (Band B-B+) that caps the step to ~12% instead of 45%.
- Pilot carveout: we can agree to a one-quarter pilot carveout with a scaled penalty (50% of standard true-up rate) — subject to legal sign-off on language.
- Quarterly true-ups: that's fine from an ops perspective; we'll need to confirm billing systems for reporting cadence but it's doable.

Looping in Laura (contracts) and Karthik (commercial counsel) to propose precise exhibit language. Karthik — can you prepare a short redline and an alternate clean exhibit for signature by EOD Thursday? That would give Jordan's committee a day to review.

Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0147

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@orionplatform.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@orionplatform.com>
Date: Wed, 21 May 2025 14:23:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Pricing exhibit — bucket alignment request

Tessa / Jordan — preliminary legal redline below. I attached a comment-annotated Word with tracked changes (exhibitB_redline_comments.docx) to make review easier. High level:

1) Transitional band: I propose a "transitional band" that applies when monthly usage falls within +/- 8% of a bucket breakpoint. During that period:
   - The effective per-token rate will be interpolated between the two bands (linear interpolation).
   - Interpolation applies for billing calculation only and does not alter minimum commitment calculations.

2) Pilot carveout: add a paragraph to Section 3(b):
   - "Customer shall be entitled to one (1) consecutive calendar quarter during the Term designated as a Pilot Quarter. During the Pilot Quarter, penalties for shortfall against the Monthly Minimum shall be reduced to fifty percent (50%) of the otherwise-applicable true-up charge. Customer must notify Provider in writing at least thirty (30) days prior to the Pilot Quarter to elect this option."

3) Quarterly true-ups: change language in Section 6 to require quarterly reconciliations, with true-up payments due within thirty (30) days after quarter close. Add audit rights limited to data relevant to billing reconciliation in that quarter.

Open items for negotiation (flagged in comments):
- Whether interpolation should be pro-rated only for the month crossing the breakpoint or applied to a rolling 30-day window. Ops prefers month-level; Jordan, if you need rolling average we can consider additional smoothing but that increases complexity.
- The notice period for Pilot Quarter — procurement asked for less than 30 days; legal prefers 30 for ops predictability. Could we meet in the middle at 14 days?

Next steps: I will export a tracked-changes PDF and a clean exhibit for signature by Thu EOD if we agree to the above mechanics. Please call out any commercial terms you need adjusted.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Commercial Counsel
Redwood Inference

Jordan — thanks, and appreciate the speed from your side.

We took Karthik's approach and prepared:
- exhibitB_redline_comments.docx (redline with comments)
- pricing_exhibit_v3.xlsx (updated with transitional band midpoints)
- exhibitB_clean_for_sig.docx (clean copy if you accept the draft)

High-level summary for your steering committee:
- Transitional band added to smooth bucket cliffs (limits immediate step to ~12%).
- One-quarter Pilot Quarter granted; Karthik proposed 30-day notice but we can compromise to 14 days if your procurement confirms.
- Quarterly true-ups with 30-day payment window; audit scope limited to billing reconciliation data.

Ask: can you confirm whether Orion prefers the 14-day or 30-day Pilot notice? If 14 days is acceptable, we will update the redline and publish the clean exhibit for signature immediately.

I can hop on a 15-minute call tomorrow morning if you want to run the slides with the committee.

Thanks — Tessa
